plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: Wild poinsettias are tall, leggy shrubs. Their fiery red bracts look like petals and surround tiny yellow flower clusters. Short winter days trigger the color change, so the bracts blaze in early December, just as the plant becomes a holiday icon.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter, with peak color from November through February
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America, where it grows in seasonally dry tropical forests
plants.funFact: The showy red parts are modified leaves called bracts, not petals. The true flowers are the small yellow structures, called cyathia, at the center.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This is a graceful evergreen shrub with glossy dark leaves. It opens delicate, silky blossoms in pink, rose and white, each with a bright boss of golden stamens. The flowers bring color to cool gardens when most other plants have gone dormant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter, typically October through December
plants.location: Native to southern Japan. Widely grown in mild-winter gardens such as the southeastern United States, the Pacific Northwest and coastal Europe
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Its seeds are pressed for a culinary and cosmetic oil in Japan.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: This Australian shrub bears bold, crimson flower heads up to 15 cm across, ringed by petal-like bracts. Each head is a dome of hundreds of tiny tubular flowers. The display is dramatic against the bushland of the Sydney sandstone country.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring into early summer in the Southern Hemisphere, mainly September to November. Some late blooms can linger into early December
plants.location: Sandstone ridges and heathland of New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: The waratah is the floral emblem of New South Wales. Its nectar-rich flower heads are pollinated by birds such as honeyeaters.
